title: random
summary: Generate random samples from a fitted or named probability distribution.

gpu_support.notes: Sampling currently uses the host RNG. A resident named-distribution parameter selects its exact owner for restored double output; structural size controls do not select output residency. Explicit parameter residency is preserved or fails terminally if the owner cannot represent the result.

description: `random(pd)` and `random(pd,sz...)` generate random samples from a `ProbabilityDistribution` object returned by `fitdist`. `random(distname,params...,sz...)` samples supported named distributions directly.
behaviors: The public named-distribution parameters and size controls are single or double. Typed-integer parameters and sizes are separate RunMat-mode extensions; parameters must be exactly representable at the binary64 distribution boundary, while sizes remain structural.
`pd` must be a fitted distribution object returned by `fitdist`, or `distname` must name a supported distribution.
`random(pd,m,n,...)` returns an array with the requested size. A vector size argument such as `[m n]` is also accepted.
Named normal, exponential, lognormal, gamma, Weibull, and Poisson distributions are supported with scalar parameters followed by optional size arguments.
Normal, exponential, lognormal, gamma, Weibull, and Poisson fitted distributions are supported.

Sampling returns double output. Host parameters produce host output, while resident named-distribution parameters restore output through the exact owning provider; broader distribution coverage, array-valued parameter expansion, and class propagation remain general API work rather than integer compatibility claims.

faqs.question: Does random support named distribution parameters?
faqs.answer: Yes for normal, exponential, lognormal, gamma, Weibull, and Poisson with scalar parameters. Distribution-specific random helpers such as `normrnd` remain available separately.
